text: I'm open to junior on-chain and data analyst roles. Over the past month, I analyzed $156.9B in high-value DEX flow across 5 chains to study protocol liquidity and wallet routing. Here is my Dune dashboard and case study: dune.com/the_olafare1 #OnChain #DataAnalytics

High volume does not equal high acquisition value. I analyzed $156.9B in DEX swaps (>= $10k) across Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, and Solana. Here is how I separated protocol noise from actionable wallet intelligence. 1/6

I started with 60,371 unique wallets across 5 chains. Base captured the largest high-value flow at $91.24B, followed by Ethereum ($11.44B) and Arbitrum ($5.48B). But the #1 address was a DEX router logging $96.77B. Volume alone creates false positives. 2/6

Next was behavioral screening. Two Solana wallets logged $983M and $720M across 53k+ and 37k+ trades in 30 days. Under my automation filter, both were flagged as high-risk bots and removed. High volume does not mean human-like. 3/6

After entity and automation filters, only 221 qualified candidate wallets survived. I segmented them by recency: Hot (<48h), Warm (2-7d), and Lapsed (8-30d) so BD teams can prioritize active market participants. 4/6

I then tested wallet outreach via Blockscan Chat, DeBank Hi, and XMTP. The takeaway: addressable does not mean reachable. Most wallets are not registered on web3 comms, creating a final-mile communication gap. 5/6

My 8-step framework: Discover → Qualify → Prioritize → Value → Incentivize → Reach → Activate → Measure. You can inspect the SQL queries and interactive Dune dashboard on my profile. 6/6 #DuneAnalytics #DeFi

A surprising result from my dataset: Base accounted for $91.24B of the $156.9B in high-value DEX flow (swaps ≥$10k) across the 5 chains analyzed. That is over 58% of all observed institutional-scale swap volume. #OnChain #Base

Why I set a ≥$10,000 swap threshold: in cross-chain DEX analysis, retail trades and micro-swaps dominate transaction count while contributing negligible protocol volume. Isolating ≥$10k trades surfaced 60,371 addresses with an average swap size of $142.8K. #SQL

How I built the entity screening query in Dune SQL: I joined dex.trades with labels.all to identify known MEV contracts, routers, and CEX deposit wallets. This allowed me to remove automated protocol noise before calculating wallet metrics. #DuneAnalytics #SQL

An important analytical limitation: observed flow is historical evidence, not guaranteed future migration. A wallet routing $20M through a DEX demonstrates capacity, but converting that flow requires structured incentives and cryptographic eligibility. #OnChain

Before focusing on on-chain data, I completed a B.A. in English Language & Literary Studies at Obafemi Awolowo University. That background trained me to examine evidence critically, question surface claims, and communicate complex data clearly. #CareerTransition

Volume without behavioral screening creates false leads. In my Solana dataset, one wallet logged $983.35M across 53,068 trades in 30 days. That is ~1,768 trades per day. It was removed from the candidate pool under my automation filter. #Solana #Analytics

Another Solana wallet logged $720.15M volume across 37,468 trades in 30 days. Despite massive volume, the trade frequency signaled algorithmic market-making or arbitrage rather than discretionary trading. Both were excluded from BD outreach. #OnChain

Lesson learned while analyzing wallet routing: venue count does not equal routing flexibility. Wallet 3cmf... interacted with 7 DEXs, yet 95.61% of its $54.43M volume went through Manifest. Looking only at DEX count would have concealed extreme incumbent lock-in.

Contrast that with Wallet Ai42...: $88.81M volume distributed across 13 DEXs (Manifest $39.33M, BisonFi $27.46M, Tessera $14.55M, Aquifer $2.29M, Jupiter $1.68M). This wallet demonstrates true multi-venue routing and is far more receptive to execution incentives.

How I built the Liquidity Impact Score: I combined 30-day volume (scale), average ticket size (execution strength), and behavioral quality (human-likelihood) into a composite metric. This prevented high-frequency low-ticket bots from outranking genuine high-value traders. #SQL

If you lead protocol growth, which wallet would you prioritize: Candidate A ($13.89M flow, 33% primary DEX share) or Candidate B ($54.43M flow, 95.6% locked into one DEX)? My scoring engine ranked Candidate A higher due to switching feasibility.

Starting with 60,371 addresses and arriving at 221 qualified candidate wallets is not a data loss—it is the entire objective of analytical qualification. Removing protocols, MEV, and routers leaves a defensible pool for protocol BD teams. #OnChainAnalytics

At Oguntechies, I built an AI-assisted Python workflow with the YouTube Data API to collect and structure prospect data across 4,000+ channels. That experience structuring data pipelines and qualifying prospects directly translates to my on-chain wallet screening work.

In my case study, I modeled opportunity from Raydium's perspective using 5% and 10% volume capture scenarios. For a wallet routing $173.75M ($146.17M on JupiterZ), capturing 5% represents $8.69M in new flow. Observed volume is evidence; capture is a scenario. #DeFi

Testing web3 outreach: I entered a target address into Blockscan Chat. The interface recognized the address and initiated a chat, but messages remain unencrypted until the recipient signs in. Address acceptance does not prove the controller will ever see the message. #Web3

Testing DeBank Hi: the target wallet was discoverable and allowed drafting a personalized BD pitch. However, sending required a $1.00 paid-send fee. This introduces real economic cost to web3 cold outreach without guaranteeing delivery or response. #OnChain

Testing XMTP: querying the target wallet returned 'Address not registered on XMTP', blocking direct message creation entirely. A public wallet address is visible on-chain, but it is not a universal messaging identity. Reachability requires prior protocol onboarding. #XMTP

The communication gap formula:

Qualified Wallets ≠ Reachable Wallets
Reachable Wallets ≠ Engaged Prospects

On-chain discovery is permissionless; human communication remains highly fragmented across wallets. #DataAnalytics

Lesson learned: The final bottleneck in protocol user acquisition is not data discovery—it is controller reachability. Building SQL queries to find $100M+ volume wallets is straightforward; establishing an authenticated communication channel is where the funnel breaks.

How is your team currently bridging the on-chain reachability gap: web3 messaging protocols (XMTP/Blockscan), on-chain transaction memos, or matching ENS/SNS handles to off-chain profiles? I'd love to hear what channels yield actual conversion.

The full wallet communication funnel I defined:

Addressable → Delivered → Visible → Attention → Response → Acquisition.

Each step has severe drop-off. Message submission is not delivery, and delivery does not guarantee controller attention. #OnChainAnalytics

I structured the qualified leads into a Top 100 Priority Queue backed by a 50-Wallet Reserve. If a target wallet fails identity or reachability checks during BD research, it is replaced from the reserve to maintain an active pipeline depth. #Growth #Analytics

In protocol growth architecture, a wallet plays a triple role:

1. Prospect ID: identifies the economic opportunity
2. Eligibility Key: gates access via smart contract allowlists
3. Attribution Key: tracks post-incentive retention and volume.

#OnChainAnalytics

Why allowlists beat manual BD: encoding qualified wallets into smart contract allowlists enables cryptographic verification of address ownership without requiring the counterparty to reveal real-world identity. This aligns with crypto-native privacy. #Web3

Why I write raw SQL on Dune rather than using packaged analytics platforms: raw SQL gives complete auditability over edge cases, transaction exclusions, and custom scoring logic. Every metric in my dashboard can be traced back to raw contract events. #SQL #DuneAnalytics

Community validation: Having protocol researchers engage with my Dune dashboard reinforced that teams need defensible, reproducible data rather than high-level vanity metrics. Data integrity builds trust. #OnChain

Key takeaway from my 5-week study: On-chain data can reveal where liquidity moves, but converting that intelligence into durable protocol growth requires multi-stage qualification, reachability infrastructure, and strict retention attribution. #DeFi #Analytics
